checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: The final video is 10 seconds long and landscape 16:9.
must.why: The assistant says the file runs 10.9 s. The clips are 858x480, which is 16:9, but the length is off by almost a second.

must.item: The supplied FitTrack home screenshot appears before the supplied workout screenshot.
must.why: Clip 1 shows the blue home screen and clip 2 shows the green workout screen.

must.item: Both screenshots remain recognizable and readable, without invented replacement UI.
must.why: The layout and colours match, but the text is garbled ('Tobry 6,240 dops', 'Wiakout'). The AI-drawn phones add an invented tab bar and status bar. The workout screen text is unreadable.
The end card frame was not provided. The assistant says it is code-drawn white text on blue.

must.item: An upbeat instrumental track is audible, with no voiceover.
must.why: The music was not heard. Audio exists with a 15 s wav and a -1 dB peak, but the mood cannot be judged.

exact_text.read_as: The end card was not shown. The only 'FitTrack' seen is the garbled in-phone header ('FitTrack' slightly distorted).

faults.what: The screen text on both phones is garbled and illegible, because the AI regenerated the UI instead of using the screenshots. This includes 'Tobry 6,240 dops' and a garbled workout list.
The AI phone invented UI elements that were not in the screenshots: a status bar, a bottom tab bar, and a cream background tint.
The runtime is 10.9 s, not 10 s.
The workout clip is shot in a different, busier set (arches, lamp, pedestal) than the home clip. The phone also looks warped and thin mid-swing.

summary: The ad has the right order, a clean look and 16:9 framing, but the screenshots were redrawn by the AI with garbled text and invented UI. The length is also 10.9 s, so a client would likely reject it.
